title: Fixed Long Hull and Open Sail Submarine
description: One independently authored whole conventional-submarine-style static exterior. A continuous long low rounded hull narrows into a pointed afterbody, while a broad full upper deck directly carries a thick capsule-plan raised sail with a genuinely open upper platform and complete floor. One whole bent solid observation-mast shape and one shorter aft mast root into that floor. Separate whole forward horizontal planes and four independently drawn aft planes meet the hull, with a shorter lower plane above the display datum. A single long rear shaft, complete tapered hub and four thick swept blunt propeller blades finish the tail. No old visible mesh or body profile is imported: this is not an open inspection-robot cage with its frame removed, nor a gas envelope with its underslung gondola moved to the top. There are no robot ducts, side engines, suspension roots, gas envelope or hanging cabin. All hull stations, deck/sail outlines, masts and planes are newly authored together. One prop zero scenes, four opaque constant PBR materials, metres and native Z up, horizontally centred whole bounds and full finite hull-bottom facets on the ground as the static display datum. Closed exterior body only, not an internal pressure vessel; the sail top is intentionally open and mast ends are opaque. No weapons, occupant, engine, reactor, valve, ballast or control-system internals. No diving, water-tightness, buoyancy, navigation, optics, propulsion, hydrodynamic performance, pressure rating, loading, manufacture, operation or marine safety claim. Rigging, animation and interaction are not made or verified.
